title: Zephyrine and the Lantern
premise: In the winter of 1917, Casper Vane keeps the lantern at Greyhaven Point and the town's only ledger of names — births, debts, the dead, the disappeared. When the army requisitions the coast and orders every record surrendered, Casper realizes the ledger is the last proof that certain people ever existed at all. Hiding it means betraying her oath to the service; surrendering it means erasing the town she promised her late husband to remember. As the great storms batter the light and an armistice rumor spreads, Casper must choose between loyalty to the institution that gave her purpose and truth to the names in her keeping. She finishes copying the ledger by hand in the lamp room on the night peace is signed, gives the original to the army, and watches the true record carried out to sea by the townsfolk who finally see her.
about_author: Rosalind Underhill is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing coastal parish records before turning to fiction. She writes from a converted net loft on the North Atlantic, where the weather does half her editing.

chapters.title: The Weight of Names
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. Establishes her routines: trimming the wick, logging ships, entering the town's names into the ledger her husband began. We learn of his death at sea two years prior and her promise to keep the record. Emotional beat: quiet grief disguised as duty; the ledger as both burden and companion.

chapters.title: Grey Boats at Dawn
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. Army vessels appear on the horizon; an officer named Lieutenant Ashcombe arrives with requisition papers for the harbor, the warehouses, and 'all civic records.' The townsfolk look to Casper, the keeper of names, for answers she doesn't have. Emotional beat: dread arriving like weather — inevitable, impersonal.

chapters.title: What the Ledger Holds
chapters.summary: Casper's POV, with flashback. She reads through the ledger at night and confronts what it contains: deserters sheltered by the town, a drowned smuggler listed as 'lost to the sea,' her own marriage entry in her husband's hand. Emotional beat: the dawning weight of what surrendering it would erase.

chapters.title: The Officer Who Reads
chapters.summary: Ashcombe's POV. He inspects the lighthouse and notices the ledger's marginalia — corrections, second entries, evidence of lives the official record contradicts. He is not cruel, only thorough, and he suspects more than he says. Emotional beat: the antagonist revealed as a mirror; he too serves a record larger than himself.

chapters.title: Storm Signal
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. The first great storm hits; a fishing boat founders and Casper keeps the light burning through the night while soldiers commandeer the boathouse. A boy from the town, Tam, helps her and sees the hidden ledger. Emotional beat: community forged in emergency; trust extended and risked.

chapters.title: Orders Come
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. Formal notice: all records to be collected within the fortnight, the lighthouse to be automated after armistice. Her identity as keeper — the only self she has left — has an expiration date. Tam offers to help copy the ledger; she refuses, then relents. Emotional beat: grief for a future being dismantled page by page.

chapters.title: The Copying
chapters.summary: Alternating Casper and Tam POV. By lamplight they transcribe names through the nights, Tam learning the town's secret history entry by entry. Ashcombe visits unexpectedly; Casper hides the original beneath the lamp's oil store. Emotional beat: intimacy of shared work; memory becoming inheritance rather than possession.

chapters.title: Betrayal or Fidelity
chapters.summary: Tam's POV. Pressured by a soldier friend, Tam nearly reveals the hiding place; instead he lies for the first time in his life and is sick with guilt. Casper discovers the near-betrayal and must decide whether trust survives. Emotional beat: the theme made flesh — loyalty and truth pulling in opposite directions.

chapters.title: The Night Before Peace
chapters.summary: Climax. Casper's POV. Armistice rumors peak; Ashcombe returns with soldiers to collect the records early. In the lamp room, storm-battered, Casper hands over the ledger — but Ashcombe, having seen the copying ink on her fingers, chooses to log it as 'destroyed by water damage' and leaves the original with her. Emotional beat: climax as moral recognition between adversaries; truth preserved by a small treachery against his own orders.

chapters.title: Lantern, Lit
chapters.summary: Resolution. Casper's POV. Peace is signed; the army withdraws. On the last night before automation, the townsfolk climb to the lamp room and Casper reads the copied ledger aloud — every name, including her husband's and, at Tam's insistence, her own. Emotional beat: invisibility ended; memory handed to the living, the light kept burning one final dawn.
